ty_text: No typhoon or storm is in the Philippine area now. Being tracked in the western Pacific: Tropical Storm Nolo is about 2,890 km northeast of Tuguegarao, moving north and holding steady. It is moving away from the Philippines. Maximum winds about 83 km/h near the centre, gusts to 120 km/h. Typhoon Koguma is about 2,940 km northeast of Virac, moving northwest and holding steady. It is getting closer to the Philippines. Maximum winds about 167 km/h near the centre, gusts to 241 km/h. Not yet confirmed: Super Typhoon Choi-Wan, 3,420 km from the nearest airport, reported by GDACS only. A cyclone is treated as confirmed, and can raise an alert, only after two sources report it.

sources: Sources: official airport weather reports (7:00 PM) and airport forecasts (issued 7:00 PM) from aviationweather.gov for 8 airports. The other 28 airports have no official airport report, so they use the MET Norway location forecast (updated 7:19 PM) and are marked Estimate. Estimates show rain and wind only and cannot confirm thunderstorms, so an Estimate airport is never shown as Danger. For Estimates, bad weather means moderate or heavy rain (2.5 mm or more in an hour), or winds of 39 km/h or more. Tomorrow and days-ahead outlooks use the same airport forecasts and MET Norway estimates and are less certain than today's alerts. Typhoon watch compares three sources, checked 7:59 PM: aviation storm warnings (position, movement, warning areas), RSMC Tokyo of the Japan Meteorological Agency (strength, how far strong winds reach, 24-hour forecast) and GDACS (cross-check). Reached at this check: aviation storm warnings, RSMC Tokyo, GDACS. A cyclone is shown and alerted only when at least two of them report it. Earthquakes are from PHIVOLCS (magnitude 4.5 and stronger), data as of Oct 10, 7:59 PM. Accuracy ranking, highest first: 1) official airport report, 2) official airport forecast, 3) official aviation area warning, 4) computer forecast estimate. The moving rain layer on the map is a MET Norway forecast, rebuilt every few hours; it is a picture of the forecast and plays no part in the alert levels. When sources differ the higher-ranked one is used, and each airport's details show its confidence. If a source cannot be reached, its backup is used automatically and the Data sources table shows which one supplied the data. Times are Philippine time. Volcanoes: ash clouds and eruptions are from official aviation ash warnings (SIGMET) on aviationweather.gov, checked 7:59 PM. Volcano alert levels are from PHIVOLCS volcano bulletins.
